candidate.title: CROP-Seq
candidate.scope: CROP-Seq (CROP-seq in the primary paper), specifically the assigned Illumina poster row using a Drop-Seq component. Inventory: a left single-cell/gRNA-Cas9-to-PolyA RNA explanatory inset; cell suspension plus colored gRNA constructs; lentiviral transduction and puromycin enrichment; an oligobead legend; cell-and-bead droplets; lysis and capture of mRNA and guide-bearing RNA; and a cDNA library labeled Transcriptome and gRNA. The inset explains reporter detectability and is represented in construct/cell features, not as a separate serial transfer into the cell suspension. Drop-Seq is an embedded operation component, not a second target method. Mosaic-Seq below, ECCITE-Seq text above and bisulfite chemistry at right belong to separate neighboring regions without a branch from CROP-Seq. This record describes the depicted implementation and its terminal readout, not all CROP-seq implementations.

operations.label: Lentiviral transduction & enrichment
operations.description: Introduce the pooled CROP guide library into the cell suspension by lentiviral transduction, then use puromycin to enrich cells carrying the construct. The output is a guide-bearing cell population that supplies transcriptome RNA and guide-containing reporter RNA for profiling.
operations.mechanism: The matched vector expresses functional hU6/Pol III guide RNA for Cas9 editing and a Pol II puromycin-resistance mRNA containing the guide sequence and a poly(A) tail. This dual transcript design explains the left gRNA/Cas9-to-PolyA RNA inset. Viral production and individual editing outcomes are not separate depicted transformations.
operations.information_effect: Perturbation identity becomes encoded in a directly detectable guide sequence within a polyadenylated transcript, rather than inferred from the Cas9 icon. Puromycin selection enriches delivery but is not a per-cell genotype measurement.
